citation.title: Interaction of tearing modes with external structures in cylindrical geometry (plasma)
citation.doi_or_arxiv: unknown (not stated in the supplied text)

topic: Analytic cylindrical theory of tearing-mode interaction with resistive walls and static error fields, covering mode locking, mode penetration and rotation braking, with tokamak scaling estimates.
own_question: How do electromagnetic and viscous torques set island width, island rotation and locking or penetration thresholds when a tearing mode interacts with external structures?
actual_method_and_evidence: The paper is analytic. It combines a Rutherford island equation with a phenomenological single-fluid viscous torque model and solves for steady-state and quasi-steady solutions. Section 8 applies an Ohmic scaling model to (2,1) modes. The author reports that the penetration threshold is about a factor of two above experiment. There is no CES, BES, ECEI, machine-learning or nowcasting content.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. The paper contains no diagnostic inputs, report targets or latency analysis.
validation_if_relevant: Not applicable. The comparison with experiment is qualitative and drawn from cited literature.
forbidden_inferences: Do not use this paper to justify pedestal-top impurity Ti nowcasting or BES/ECEI informativeness.
Do not cite the Section 8 scaling model as a validated KSTAR prediction.
Do not imply that any rotation physics here underlies our estimators.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The paper concerns MHD tearing-mode and error-field rotation physics, not CES temperature estimation. Its link to impurity rotation and temperature is indirect, and citing it would suggest a physical mechanism that our study does not identify.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
